title: Faangscape - Card battler with poker combos free to play on web
author: DangerStonks
selftext:
[https://faangscape.com/](https://faangscape.com/)

Faangscape is a fantasy card battler based on poker hands with a tech company theme. I work for a FAANG company. I had this game in my head for years. Then image diffusion models got really good about two years ago, and I made physical cards that I printed for my friends. Then about 5 days ago, I decided to turn it into a video game, because Opus 5.5 is magic.

You can play against game AI or friends. Here's how I did it:

* Code: Claude Code agents built the C# rules engine, the Unity client and the online server.
* Balance: a simulator plays thousands of AI-vs-AI games to tune the cards. My printed game was actually pretty close, but I didn't have anyone to play thousands of games with. :)
* Art: AI images are OpenAI. Voices are ElevenLabs, music is Lyria. 3D models are Tripo.
* Trailer: rendered from JavaScript, with real gameplay captures, Kling for the moving card art, and Gemini reviewing each cut as art director.

Please play the game, let me know if its any fun and if I should keep working on it. If its any good, should I put it on Steam? Would love your thoughts.

comments.author: Opening_Wafer_6584
comments.body:
Hey, Alex here from Tripo. Really cool project, especially the speed you’ve moved at from physical cards to a playable online game.

I also like how modular the stack is: Claude for code, simulation for balance, OpenAI for art, Tripo for the 3D side, and then a separate trailer pipeline on top.

Would be interested to hear which 3D assets you’re using Tripo for right now and whether they’re mainly cosmetic/presentation assets or part of the actual gameplay experience.

Definitely seems worth continuing if you’re still enjoying the iteration loop.
